mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a term premium compression effect, lowering expected discount rates and thereby pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 25 bps within the same month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-trigger mean (t-test p > 0.05), or term premium proxies (e.g., 10Y Treasury real yield) show no significant compression.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below the prior 12-month average indicate disinflation, which reduces policy rate expectations and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls continuously for three consecutive months below its 12-month rolling average
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns under such triggers are not statistically outperforming a baseline of 0.5% over 12 months, or alternative inflation proxies (e.g., PCE) show no consistent deceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10,000 jobs in a single month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Across 20 triggered events, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or alternative labor indicators (e.g., JOLTS) show no correlation with the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in inventories (implied via RSAFS) suggests supply-side stress, which elevates risk premia and produces negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 5% in a month while RSAFS falls by at least 10% from the prior month
failure_condition: In 20 such triggered events, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or alternative supply proxies (e.g., Durable Goods Orders) fail to confirm the pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) above trend for three consecutive months indicates resilient consumer demand, which lowers financing costs and supports positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds its 12-month linear trend by at least 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns under such triggers average no more than 0.5% above a neutral baseline (0%), or alternative demand proxies (e.g., personal consumption expenditures) show no consistent pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals a cooling labor market, which increases risk aversion and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% by at least 0.3 percentage points within a month
failure_condition: Over 10 such triggers, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or alternative labor indicators (e.g., job openings) do not show a corresponding decline.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of negative real yields on 10-year Treasuries (implied by a persistent decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.5%) increases the present value of future cash flows, generating positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns under such conditions do not exceed +0.75% above a neutral 60-day benchmark (based on 10Y real yield), or alternative real yield proxies (e.g., 10Y Treasury real rate) show no convergence.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) followed within the same month by a rise in supply-chain disruptions (indirectly captured by RSAFS volatility) creates uncertainty that elevates market risk premia and produces negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 8% in a month and RSAFS volatility (standard deviation) increases by at least 15% from the prior month
failure_condition: Across 10 such triggered events, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or alternative supply disruption indicators (e.g., shipping delays) fail to correlate with the signal.
